title: Turkish pronunciation (practical summary)
summary: Turkish is highly phonemic: most letters map to one sound, and every vowel is pronounced. The first priorities are the eight-vowel system, vowel harmony, and consonant letters that differ from English. Learn ı as a back, unrounded, short vowel (not /i/), and ö/ü as front rounded vowels with lip rounding. Turkish has no diphthongs: pronounce adjacent vowels separately. Vowel harmony controls suffixes: front vowels (e, i, ö, ü) usually take front-vowel suffixes, back vowels (a, ı, o, u) take back-vowel suffixes; rounded/unrounded also matters. Stress is usually on the final syllable, but place names and some suffixes shift it, so copy native stress rather than using English stress. Do not reduce unstressed vowels to schwa. Consonants: c = /dʒ/, ç = /tʃ/, ş = /ʃ/, j = /ʒ/; ğ is mostly silent and lengthens the preceding vowel; r is a short tap, not the English approximant. Final b, d, c, g devoice to p, t, ç, k in native words (kitap, kanat), so do not add voicing. Link words smoothly and keep long vowels in loanwords distinct. Common traps are replacing ı with /i/, ignoring vowel harmony, pronouncing ğ as hard g, and using English stress and vowel reduction.

sounds.name: dotless i
sounds.how: Back, unrounded, short vowel; tongue pulled back, lips spread. It is not English /i/ and not schwa.

sounds.name: front rounded o
sounds.how: Front vowel with rounded lips, similar to the vowel in French 'peu' but more open; no direct English equivalent.

sounds.name: front rounded u
sounds.how: High front vowel with rounded lips, like saying /i/ while rounding the lips; no direct English equivalent.

sounds.name: soft g
sounds.how: Usually silent; it lengthens the preceding vowel. Between front vowels it may sound like a light y.

sounds.name: ce
sounds.how: Voiced postalveolar affricate /dʒ/, like English j in 'jam'.

sounds.name: çe
sounds.how: Voiceless postalveolar affricate /tʃ/, like English ch in 'chair'.

sounds.name: şe
sounds.how: Voiceless postalveolar fricative /ʃ/, like English sh in 'ship'.

sounds.name: re
sounds.how: Alveolar tap [ɾ], like the tt in American English 'butter' or a single Spanish r.

common_mistakes: Replacing ı with /i/ or /ʌ/ (e.g. ılık as 'ilik').
Pronouncing ö and ü without lip rounding, so göz sounds like 'gez' and gül like 'gil'.
Ignoring vowel harmony when adding suffixes.
Pronouncing ğ as a hard English g.
Using English stress and reducing unstressed vowels to schwa.
Pronouncing c as /k/ or /s/ instead of /dʒ/.
Using an English r instead of a short tap.
Voicing final b, d, c, g where Turkish devoices them (kitap, kanat).
